definitions.explanation: The time at nine hours past midnight or noon.

examples.japanese: {九時|くじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{着|つ}く→着く：00680_tsuku⟧。
examples.english: I arrive at the office at nine o'clock.
The store opens at nine in the morning.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{九時|くじ}な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦まだ→まだ：00603_mada⟧⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦しています→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Even though it's nine at night, I'm still working.

notes:
{九時|くじ} is the standard way to say "nine o'clock." Note that {九|く} uses the on'yomi reading, not きゅう, when telling time.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧{九時|くじ}: 9 a.m.
- ⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧{九時|くじ}: 9 p.m.
- {九時半|くじはん}: 9:30
- {九時|くじ}⟦ちょうど→ちょうど：02916_choudo⟧: exactly 9 o'clock
- {九時|くじ}{過|す}ぎ: past nine o'clock
- ⟦{午前|ごぜん}→午前：00548_gozen⟧{九時|くじ}: 9:00 AM (formal)

PRONUNCIATION:
In telling time, {九|く}じ (not きゅうじ). This matches the pattern where {九|く} is used in ⟦{九月|くがつ}→九月：00646_kugatsu⟧ (September) and ⟦{九日|ここのか}→九日：02901_kokonoka⟧ uses the native Japanese reading.
